quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hungarian paprika, Hungary's most famous spice, comes in eight different varieties ranging from delicate and sweet to fiery hot. The town of Kalocsa has been growing and grinding paprika peppers since the 16th century, and the spice is so important to Hungarian culture that it has its own museum!

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Harbor Seals
short_read.teaser: Harbor seals in the Strait of Juan de Fuca are more social than we thought, with mothers teaching their pups the best fishing spots. Learn about the fascinating behaviors of these charming marine mammals right in your backyard.

medium_read.title: How Plants Talk to Each Other
medium_read.teaser: Scientists have discovered that plants communicate through underground fungal networks, sharing nutrients and even warning each other about pests. This hidden world beneath our gardens is more connected and alive than we ever imagined.

long_read.title: The Forgotten Female Botanists Who Changed Science
long_read.teaser: From the Amazon rainforest to the mountains of Tibet, women explorers collected and documented plants that became the foundation of modern botany. Their stories of courage, curiosity, and dedication are finally being told.

port_angeles.title: Butterfly Season at Hurricane Ridge
port_angeles.description: Late summer is prime time to spot beautiful butterflies at Hurricane Ridge, including the Clodius Parnassian with its delicate white wings. These high-altitude butterflies dance among the wildflowers on sunny days, making the subalpine meadows even more magical. The cooler mornings of late August are perfect for a gentle visit.

puzzle_1.question: The Olympic Peninsula receives about ___ feet of rain per year in its rainforest areas, making it one of the wettest places in the continental United States.
puzzle_1.correct_response: That's right, Barbara! The Hoh Rainforest gets about 12 feet of rainfall each year — that's why everything is so lush and green!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! The rainforest gets about 12 feet of rain annually — enough to create those magical moss-covered trees!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: The Olympic rainforests receive about 12 feet of rain each year — that incredible rainfall creates the beautiful, misty green world we love!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: The Hoh Rainforest is one of the largest temperate rainforests in the U.S., where massive Sitka spruces and western hemlocks are draped in thick carpets of moss thanks to all that Pacific moisture.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful, Ildiko! Pillangó is indeed butterfly — such a lovely, musical word!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó' — doesn't it sound just as delicate as the creature itself?
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is a unique language in Europe, part of the Finno-Ugric family rather than the Indo-European languages around it. Many Hungarian words, like pillangó, have a musical, flowing quality.

puzzle_3.question: What do hummingbirds use to remember which flowers they've already visited?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Yes! Hummingbirds have remarkable spatial memory and can remember every flower they've visited, when they visited it, and when it will have nectar again. Such intelligent little creatures!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: Hummingbirds rely on their excellent spatial memory to track which flowers they've visited. They can remember thousands of flowers and know exactly when each one will have fresh nectar!
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Hummingbirds have the largest brain-to-body ratio of any bird, and they can remember migration routes, feeding sites, and individual flowers for years. Some can recall thousands of flowers and when each one will refill with nectar.
